text:
sam: Raven Health reported a big regression — 4x p99 and throughput drop on prod after the runtime deploy. Customers hitting timeouts.
maya: ack. can you paste customer topology (region, model, avg seq, route)?
sam: region: us-west-2, model: open-7b-quant, avg_seq: ~1024, route: /v1/generate, dedicated pool: raven-prod-1
sam: example error the customer sees: "request timed out after 30s". baseline p99 ~1.8s -> observed 5.6s. throughput down ~45%.
tess: do we have a deploy id? @deploy-bot any context?
deploy-bot: raven-runtime-service deployed by ci (sha: a1b2c3d) at 2025-03-14T18:12:03Z to raven-prod-1
li: I noticed a kernel-selector tweak in that sha — could be falling back to slower kernels for long sequences. can we repro on an isolated shard?
maya: @li yes. @sam can you ask the customer for traces (flamegraphs/traces) and kv cache metrics?
sam: asking customer now. in parallel can we run a bench from our infra to reproduce? @bench-bot recommended cmd?
bench-bot: recommended loadtest command: 
./bench --target https://raven-api.prod --concurrency 64 --seq 1024 --duration 300 --model open-7b-quant --route /v1/generate --samples 5000
li: also grab kernel-selector logs and kernel list: /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log and /var/log/runtime/kernels.txt
nora: pinging infra to spin an ephemeral pool to avoid impacting prod.
infra: ephemeral pool raven-debug-23 created (instance: g5.12xlarge)
maya: run the bench against raven-debug-23 and collect kv cache hit rates, GPU util, and per-token latency histogram.
sam: customer uploaded traces: https://files.redwood/raven/trace-2191234567.json — notes 3 p99 spikes at t+120s, t+207s, t+305s
li: quick scan: spikes align with kernel swap events in kernel-selector.log snippet: 
```
2025-03-14T18:12:35Z kernel-selector: swapped kernel open7_kernel_2 -> open7_kernel_fallback latency 18ms
2025-03-14T18:12:36Z kernel-selector: fallback hit rate 12%
```
sam: can we mitigate by reverting the selector change?
maya: short-term mitigation: revert selector policy for raven-prod-1. @tess can you run a canary rollback and monitor?
tess: initiating canary rollback now. command: 
```
rctl rollback --service raven-runtime --shard raven-prod-1 --to-sha a1b2b2c
```
deploy-bot: rollback started at 2025-03-14T19:05:12Z
nora: bench against debug pool BEFORE change: p99 ~1.9s under same load. AFTER change p99 ~5.2s and tail spikes match production.
li: uploaded flamegraphs and KV heatmap to the perf bucket: https://files.redwood/perf/raven/2191234567/* 
li: root cause hypothesis: fallback kernels are not optimized for long context lengths (1024) and cause KV cache miscaching leading to extra GPU work. need kernel tuning + selector policy guardrails.
maya: immediate plan: (1) keep rollback until fix verified, (2) add long-seq unit tests for selector, (3) tune fallback kernels and add perf regression checks. @li can you drive (2) and (3)? assign nora for infra test runs.
li: taking ownership — will open perf PR with test harness and assign nora for CI infra runs. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
sam: updated customer: rollback in progress, perf team investigating, ETA for fix ~48-72 hrs. they requested an ETA for a permanent fix.
maya: give customer rollback progress + approx timeline; we'll follow up with postmortem if rollback completes and data looks good.
sam: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback finished at 2025-03-14T19:08:40Z status: success
tess: monitoring metrics now — p99 trending back to baseline :eyes:
sam: customer confirms latency improving and throughput recovering. closing the loop.
